name: Hangzhou
coordinates_source: West Lake centre, OSM relation 2308774 (visitor hub of the city)
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a Hangzhou city page whose See section lists West Lake, Lingyin Temple, Leifeng Pagoda, Longjing and Xixi; West Lake is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Hangzhou a headline Chinese destination (Wikipedia/Wikivoyage "Hangzhou").
reason: Rank 2: a national highlight in guidebooks, the Jiangnan city built around West Lake. 42 kept spots, far above the four-spot bar. Span 80 km covers Yuhang, Xiaoshan, Binjiang and the near Fuyang and Lin'an districts.

name: Huzhou
coordinates_source: Lianhuazhuang/Wuxing city point from candidates (Wuxing district centre); pin stage to confirm against OSM place=city
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Huzhou" city/prefecture page that lists the Huzhou Museum, Lianhuazhuang and Changxing sights (Chinese Alligator Village).
reason: 5 kept spots (Huzhou Museum, Lianhuazhuang Park, Brush Museum, Gu Zhu Mountain, Chinese Alligator Village), above the four-spot bar. Rank 4: a prefecture city that guidebooks cover but not a headline; Anji, Nanxun and Moganshan are separate named bases. Overlap checked against Anji, Nanxun, Hangzhou: centres >33 km apart.

name: Anji
coordinates_source: centre of the Anji spots (county seat Dipu and Tianhuangping); pin stage to confirm
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has an "Anji" page covering the county: Bamboo Exposition Park, Great Bamboo Sea, Yunshang ski resort; Anji is a tourism brand ("China Bamboo Town").
reason: 8 kept spots, a county travellers name (bamboo sea, Tianhuangping). Rank 4: worth a detour from Hangzhou/Shanghai. Moganshan (Deqing, ~22 km E) is outside Anji and stays standalone.

name: Jiaxing
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Jiaxing' city page with See/Do (South Lake, Meiwan, Yuehe); prefecture-level city, rail stop between Shanghai and Hangzhou
note: Centre approximated between South Lake (30.7568,120.7557) and Jiaxing Museum; no source for a city-centre point beyond that, pin stage to confirm. Wuzhen 28 km west, outside metro.

name: Wuzhen
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Wuzhen' (Jiaxing/Tongxiang), 5A water town, Wikipedia 27,290 views/yr; headline trip in itself (Dongzha, Xizha, Mao Dun)
note: Only 3 spots: justified by the headline-attraction clause (a trip in itself), not the four-spot bar; Wuzhen itself is the destination so no 'Wuzhen' wrapper spot. Not Jiangnan Water Towns (Jiangsu): ~65 km from its centre. Fall back to three standalone spots if the owner rejects.

name: Jinhua
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Jinhua" page (the prefecture) whose See section lists Shiwang Mansion, Shuanglong Cave and Jinhua Mountain; Wikipedia "Jinhua".
reason: Regional city and base with 4 kept spots (Shuanglong Cave, Architecture Park, Jinhua Mountain, Shiwang Mansion), meeting the four-spot bar. Rank 5: a local hub, not a national draw. Span 40 km covers the urban Wucheng/Jindong area; Lanxi, Dongyang, Yiwu and Yongkang are separate county-level cities and their spots stay standalone.

name: Wuyi Hot Springs
coordinates_source: English Wikipedia "Wuyi County, Zhejiang" article coordinates (county seat)
name_evidence: Wikipedia "Wuyi County, Zhejiang" and Wikivoyage has a "Wuyi" page; China Daily Jinhua presents Wuyi (hot springs, ancient villages, Danxia scenery) as a two-day tour and the Wuyi Hot Springs as a tourism brand. Weak: a county name, also shared with the Fujian Wuyi Mountains, so the owner may rename it "Wuyi Hot Springs" or fold it.
reason: 8 kept spots clustered in one county (hot springs, Ming-Qing villages, Danxia, forest park, old town, family farm): above the four-spot bar, and no larger named region (Jinhua is 25 km away with a different draw) holds them. Rank 5.
rename_note: skeptic lean; owner has not chosen between rename and folding into Jinhua

name: Longquan
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a Longquan page (outline: celadon and swords, a city in Zhejiang)
reason: 5 kept spots (celadon kiln site, celadon museum, sword factory and museum, Baishanzu). Baishanzu is a national park under construction with one kept spot, so it is a spot of Longquan, not a destination.
coordinates_source: centre = Longquan Celadon Museum point (Candidates, in Longquan town); refine from OSM place=town at research

name: Ningbo
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Ningbo' city page lists See/Do sections for the city and surroundings; major port city on guidebook itineraries

name: Xikou
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Xikou' page (Chiang Kai-shek's hometown, Xuedou Mountain); China Daily Ningbo lists 'Xikou-Tengtou Tourist Area' (5A); Xikou itself is the destination, not a spot
note: 33 km from Ningbo centre, centres farther than 0.75x larger radius; outside Ningbo urban metro

name: Quzhou
coordinates_source: OSM place=city relation (Quzhou); city centre point
name_evidence: China Daily Quzhou government tourism pages use 'Quzhou' as the heading for its ancient city, Confucius South Family Temple and Lanke Mountain; English Wikipedia 'Quzhou' (~18k views/yr); Wikivoyage Zhejiang lists it as a city. Wikivoyage has no own Quzhou page (judge note).
reason: Prefecture-level city and regional hub with seven kept spots in and around it; rank 4 (worth a detour, not a national top-tier draw).

name: Jiangshan
coordinates_source: Centre between Mount Jianglang (OSM peak) and its village/pass cluster; not from memory of a town centre
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Jiangshan' page and the Wikivoyage Zhejiang region page (counted); China Daily gov Jiangshan one-day itinerary listing Jianglang Mountain, Nianbadu, Qingyang and Xianxia Pass. Named for the county-level city which travellers use as the base for Jianglang Mountain.
reason: Four kept spots around the Jiangshan base (Mount Jianglang, Nianbadu, Qingyang Village, Xianxia Pass); the town Jiangshan itself is the gateway, not a separate spot beside its own attractions.

name: Shaoxing
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Shaoxing / Lu Xun precinct geo tag (old-town centre)
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Shaoxing' city page with See/Do listings; guidebook chapter, 'Venice of the East' water-town brand

name: Taizhou
coordinates_source: proxy: Taizhou Museum, Jiaojiang (Wikipedia); city-centre point to be resolved from an OSM place=city node
name_evidence: English Wikivoyage has a page "Taizhou (Zhejiang)" listing See/Do entries; the prefecture-level city of Jiaojiang, Huangyan and Luqiao.
reason: Four kept places (Taizhou Museum, Ocean World, Jiufeng Mountain, Fonte Wild Mainland) inside the urban area (Fonte ~21 km, Jiufeng ~13 km from centre, within 75% of a 60 km span). Zhejiang's Taizhou, not Jiangsu's. Rank 5: local hub.

name: Yandang Mountains
name_evidence: Wikivoyage Wenzhou lists 'Yandang Mountains' as a headline See entry with the sub-areas Lingfeng, Lingyan, Dalongchu and Sanzhe; English Wikipedia article 'Yandang Mountains' (national scenic area, ~6,000 views/yr).
reason: Named headline scenic area with four kept sub-area spots; ranked 3 (regional favourite, not a national top-tier draw).

name: Mount Putuo
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a Putuoshan page (and Zhoushan page listing it); Buddhist sacred island, one of four sacred Buddhist mountains of China, national park.
reason: Six kept spots on the island itself (Puji, South Sea Guanyin, Fayu, Huiji, Foding Mountain, Hundred Step Beach), above the four-spot bar; rank 3 honestly, a famous pilgrimage island but not a top-two country highlight. Span 15 km covers the 8.6 km island. Zhoushan is not proposed as a region destination: the islands are separate ferry bases spread over ~150 km, so a region span would balloon.
